title: Viṣṇu strode out this world

words.context: Sāyaṇa: in the dusty place of the foot; Bhāskara: the worlds are the dust in his footprint

morphology.note: from tri with the suffix -dhā (Bhāskara and Sāyaṇa cite P. 5.3.46 (एधाच्च) for the form).
pāṃsu, ‘dust’, with the possessive suffix -ra. In the Saṃhitā the verse runs on into the next and the word is पाँसुर; recited alone it takes its pausal form (a logged correction).

translation.literal: Viṣṇu strode out this; threefold he set down his step; [all] is gathered in his dusty [footprint].
translation.readable: Viṣṇu strode out across this world; three times he set down his foot, and all of it is held in the dust of his footprint.

meaning: The verse of Viṣṇu’s three strides (RV 1.22.17; TS 1.2.13.1). Viṣṇu strode across this world, setting down his foot three times, and the whole world is held in the dust of his footprint. Bhāskara takes the three steps as earth, mid-air and heaven, and the dust as the worlds themselves, gathered in the lotus of his foot; Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda, names Viṣṇu as the one who took the form of Trivikrama and cites Yāska’s discussion of the three places. In the Saṃhitā the verse belongs to the building of the havirdhāna, the shed for the soma carts: an offering is made in the track of the southern cart’s wheel. The verse addresses Viṣṇu.
in_the_rite: The second mantra of Budha’s step in the Navagraha sūktam (witness S). S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together, so the edition does not say which this verse is for; the verse itself addresses Viṣṇu. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara gives its use in the Saṃhitā: «दक्षिणस्यां चक्रवर्तिन्यां जुहोति» — an offering in the track of the southern wheel.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa quotes the Kalpa: going round behind the southern havirdhāna cart, «दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य पश्चाद् अक्षम् उपसृप्य», the priest offers in the wheel-track with this verse.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara: Viṣṇu is the pervading lord, «व्यापी भगवान्»; the three steps are «पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवि चेत्याधारभेदेन पदस्य त्रैविध्यम्» — earth, mid-air and heaven.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda: «विष्णुः त्रिविक्रमावतारधारी» — Viṣṇu who took the form of Trivikrama — set down his foot in three ways.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A gāyatrī (eight syllables to the pāda); the Saṃhitā prints its first two pādas as one line.
